The Templar III is a Dark Age era eighty-five ton assault OmniMech produced by General Motors for the Federated Suns. Introduced around 3100, it was designed as a direct replacement for the original Templar after the destruction of Kallon Industries' factory on Talon during the Jihad eliminated production of the first-generation design. General Motors established a new production line on New Valencia to continue the Templar legacy with updated technologies.

Like its predecessor, the Templar III serves primarily as a command 'Mech for AFFS assault formations. The design incorporates advanced equipment across its alternate configurations, giving field commanders significant tactical flexibility while maintaining the assault-weight presence that made the original Templar an effective formation anchor.

The most significant change from the original Templar is the Templar III's adoption of a GM 340 Light engine in place of the KalTek 340 Extralight. This substantially improves survivability by eliminating the vulnerability to side torso destruction that plagued the original design, though it comes at the cost of reduced pod space, dropping from forty tons to twenty-nine. The Kallon Type XX Endo Steel chassis and StarGuard CIV armor maintain the same level of protection as the predecessor, and a Heavy-Duty Gyro improves stability under fire.

The primary configuration draws comparison to the proven WHM-8D Warhammer loadout, mounting twin ER PPCs as its primary armament alongside extended-range medium and small lasers. A four-tube short-range missile launcher provides supplementary close-range firepower, with CASE protecting the ammunition. A targeting computer links all energy weapons for improved accuracy, while four additional double heat sinks manage the considerable thermal output of the energy-heavy weapons suite.

While the reduced pod capacity limits the Templar III's ability to mount the heaviest weapon loadouts, the improved chassis durability ensures it can remain in the fight longer. Several configurations take advantage of advanced and Clan-specification technologies to maximize firepower within the tighter weight budget, making the Templar III a more resilient, if somewhat less versatile, successor to the original.

The Templar III's development grew directly from the ashes of the Jihad. With the Kallon Industries factory on Talon destroyed by the Word of Blake, the Federated Suns lost its only production source for the original Templar. General Motors on New Valencia, already producing the Pendragon, a limited-production design loosely based on the Templar chassis, leveraged their familiarity with the platform to develop a modernized successor. Production of the Templar III began around 3100, establishing New Valencia as the new center of Templar-lineage manufacturing.

The Templar III quickly became a popular command 'Mech for AFFS company and battalion commanders, appearing regularly in assault lances throughout Federated Suns frontline formations. During the Capellan invasion campaigns of the Dark Age, lances of Templar IIIs proved effective in combined arms operations. In one notable engagement on Spica in late 3144, a lance of three Templar IIIs and a Salamander inflicted significant casualties on a Capellan 'Mech company, using ER PPCs and targeting computers to devastating effect while channeling the enemy through minefields and narrow streets.

The Templar III's influence extended beyond the Federated Suns. When General Motors resumed Victor production in the 3080s, they redesigned that venerable assault 'Mech to share many components with the Templar III, creating manufacturing efficiencies on New Valencia. Additionally, the custom configuration piloted by the First Prince demonstrated the platform's ability to accept Clan-specification weaponry, producing a significantly more lethal variant that served through the critical campaigns of the late 3140s and into the ilClan era.

The Templar was the first unique Federated Suns OmniMech, an eighty-five ton assault design produced by Kallon Industries and introduced in 3062. Commissioned to address the Federated Suns' lack of an indigenous OmniMech design, the Templar was intended to replace aging designs like the Awesome and Victor in frontline units.

Built around proven off-the-shelf components to reduce costs and speed development, the design offered a generous forty tons of pod space for mission-specific configurations, establishing itself as a powerful and versatile command platform for AFFS assault formations. Though production was eventually disrupted, the Templar proved durable enough to remain in active service well beyond its original production run.

The Templar is built on a lightweight Kallon Type XIX Endo Steel chassis and powered by a KalTek 340 Extralight engine, achieving a respectable top speed of sixty-four kilometers per hour for its weight class. Sixteen and a half tons of Starshield A armor provide excellent protection, while CASE in the right torso mitigates ammunition explosion risks. Thirteen fixed double heat sinks manage the baseline thermal load, leaving the full forty tons of pod space available for weapons and equipment.

The primary configuration emphasizes multi-range engagement capability. A Gauss rifle provides devastating long-range firepower, while a large pulse laser, medium pulse laser, and two extended-range medium lasers deliver punishing damage at closer distances. A Streak SRM-4 launcher exploits armor breaches, and an advanced targeting computer links the Gauss rifle and all lasers for enhanced accuracy. This combination makes the Prime an effective battlefield command platform capable of engaging threats at virtually any range.

The Templar's primary vulnerability lies in its reliance on an Extralight engine, which leaves it susceptible to destruction from torso penetration. However, the design philosophy accepted this trade-off to maximize the available pod space, giving field commanders exceptional flexibility in tailoring the 'Mech to specific mission requirements.

The Templar's origins trace directly to the political tensions within the Federated Commonwealth following the Great Refusal in 3060. While both Archon-Prince Victor Steiner-Davion and his sister Archon Katrina dismissed calls for OmniMech development on economic grounds, Field Marshal Duke George Hasek of the Capellan March took matters into his own hands. Hasek directly commissioned Kallon Industries on Talon, a moon of Wernke, to develop the design, backing the project with his own considerable personal fortune. The resulting 'Mech entered production in 3062, just as the FedCom Civil War was erupting.

With House Hasek as the driving force behind its creation, the Templar's initial distribution was heavily weighted toward Capellan March formations. The first units off Kallon's production lines were routed to the Syrtis Fusiliers, with subsequent production runs reaching units such as the Federated Suns Armored Cavalry and the Davion Assault Guards. Throughout the Civil War, Hasek's loyalists ensured these powerful OmniMechs were directed exclusively to units opposing Archon Katrina, particularly excluding Loyalist commands from receiving any. The Twenty-Second Avalon Hussars received several during their defense of Talon, though this alone proved insufficient to secure victory.

The Word of Blake Jihad dealt a catastrophic blow to the Templar program when the Kallon Industries factory on Talon was vaporized, halting all production. The design's intended rise as a flagship AFFS assault 'Mech was set back by decades. General Motors, having obtained access to the Templar's design data through Operation MUSE RED, eventually established production on New Valencia, though they chose to develop a modernized successor rather than restart the original line.

During the Republic era, the Republic Institute of Strategic Combat developed the experimental ORISC configuration, fitting stored Templar chassis with RISC Repeating TSEMP weapons and other volatile experimental technology. The Republic of the Sphere and its wartime Exarch deployed these in false-flag operations under AFFS colors against the Capellan Confederation and Draconis Combine. When Julian Davion visited Terra in 3146, nearly all stored ORISC equipment packages were included in supplies provided to the AFFS, where they saw continued use until every piece of the experimental gear was destroyed through combat, wear, or self-detonation by the end of the 3140s.

Despite the loss of its original production line, surviving Templars remained in AFFS service throughout the Dark Age and into the ilClan era, valued for their durability, flexibility, and the Easy to Maintain quirk that kept aging chassis operational far beyond their expected service life. The Blessed Order's revived First Division also operated a modified configuration, the BLO variant, incorporating improved C3 networking to coordinate their reformed ComStar forces.

The Tenshi, whose name translates to "Angel" in Japanese, is a 95-ton assault OmniMech introduced in 3101 by Luthien Armor Works for the Draconis Combine Mustered Soldiery. Designed to be manufactured entirely from Combine-sourced technologies and materials, the Tenshi represented LAW's first foray into OmniMech production for the DCMS. Conceived during a period of covert rearmament following the Jihad, the design answered the Combine's need for a domestically produced assault-weight platform that did not rely on foreign supply chains. A common sight among the Dragon's assault formations, the Tenshi fills the heavy end of the weight spectrum with a flexible platform capable of adapting to multiple battlefield roles through its substantial modular pod system.

The Tenshi was Luthien Armor Works' first OmniMech platform to incorporate several advanced technologies that had entered production in the decades preceding the Jihad. Built on an Endo-Composite internal structure and powered by a Hermes 285 Light fusion engine, the design achieves a remarkable 48 tons of pod capacity, roughly half its total weight. This impressive payload comes at the cost of speed, with a maximum velocity of only 54 kilometers per hour, particularly slower than many comparable assault designs of the era. A Compact Gyro saves additional internal volume, while 18.5 tons of Mitchell Argon Standard armor provides exceptional protection across all locations.

The Tenshi is somewhat labor-intensive to reconfigure due to its complex pod linkage system, making rapid battlefield swaps impractical during time-sensitive operations. This logistical burden is the design's most significant drawback, requiring dedicated technical teams and extended maintenance windows that can strain a formation's operational tempo during fast-moving campaigns.

The Tenshi emerged from Luthien Armor Works as part of a deliberate and covert program to reconstitute the Draconis Combine's shattered military in the aftermath of the Jihad. While publicly adhering to Devlin Stone's disarmament agreements, the Combine quietly pursued new BattleMech projects that would achieve two purposes: manufacture designs using Combine-centric technologies, and rapidly rebuild its decimated 'Mech regiments. Older machines were cycled down to planetary militias to maintain the appearance of compliance while new hardware flowed to frontline units.

The DCMS initially assigned the first Tenshis to the Ghost Regiments, a deliberate choice rooted in both pragmatism and politics. The Ghost Regiments' lower profile within the DCMS meant that should the Tenshi prove a tactical failure, much as the Daboku had nearly a century earlier, the embarrassment would be contained within less prestigious formations. Ghost pilots, however, quickly embraced the new OmniMech and realized its battlefield potential.

In 3103, the Tenshi saw one of its earliest significant engagements when the First Ghost dropped two lances of the assault 'Mechs on the Ghost Bear Dominion world of Grumium. The raiding force struck directly at a weapons stockpile, blasting through a Striker Star before encountering heavier resistance from a Dominion Nova of the First Freemen Cluster. When the Bear commander refused a Trial of Possession, the Ghosts employed massed firepower to devastating effect, cutting down Clan 'Mechs while absorbing heavy return fire. Six of the eight Tenshis survived the engagement and returned to the Combine along with several hundred tons of captured Clan technology, a significant haul that validated the design's combat worthiness.

By the mid-thirty-second century, the Tenshi had become a common sight among the Dragon's frontline 'Mech regiments. At least one full assault company within the Sixteenth Galedon Regulars fielded the type exclusively, demonstrating growing production numbers and the DCMS' deepening confidence in the design. The Tenshi's combination of heavy armor, massive pod capacity, and the flexibility inherent to OmniMech technology ensured its continued prominence within Combine formations as tensions escalated across the Inner Sphere.

The Thanatos was developed by StarCorps Industries as a seventy-five ton OmniMech intended to emulate the Clan Summoner. After years of producing licensed OmniMechs from Luthien Armor Works on four worlds in the Federated Commonwealth and St. Ives Compact, StarCorps had gained sufficient expertise to design their own Omni-technology platforms by 3060. When neither the LAAF nor the AFFS expressed interest in another OmniMech design, citing high costs and the availability of existing models, StarCorps converted the Thanatos into a standard BattleMech. This pragmatic decision won contracts from both militaries beginning in 3061.

Produced at StarCorps facilities on Crofton and Loburg, the Thanatos filled the role of a heavy cavalry platform, offering a blend of speed, firepower, and electronic warfare capability that kept it in production through the Jihad, Dark Age, and into the ilClan era.

Taking design cues from the Clan Thor, the Thanatos is built on a StarFrame Heavy Endo Steel chassis and powered by a PlasmaStar 375 Extra Light engine, giving it a top speed of 86 kph, fast for a heavy BattleMech. Five Audi-Fokker Mark IV jump jets provide an additional 150 meters of jumping capability. The internal components and electronics systems are heavily reinforced and stabilized, giving the chassis excellent resistance to rough terrain and combat impacts. Thirteen tons of Durallex Heavy armor provide solid protection for its weight class, though the extra-light engine remains a vulnerability if either side torso is breached.

The weapons array is weighted toward medium and short range engagements. A Defiance Model 6 extended-range large laser provides long-range reach, while a Shigunga MRM-20 launcher and two Defiance Model XII extended-range medium lasers deliver punishing firepower at closer ranges. A RAMTech 800P medium pulse laser adds accurate close-range fire. A Guardian ECM suite disrupts enemy electronics, while a C3 slave unit dramatically improves accuracy when operating as part of a networked lance.

The Tian-Zong was introduced in 3090 as a dedicated command BattleMech for the Capellan Confederation Armed Forces. Developed by Hellespont 'Mech Works on Sian in cooperation with the Capellan Science Foundation, the design was originally intended as a mobile fire support platform for the Confederation's shadow lances. Combining potent Gauss-based firepower with sophisticated stealth technology and an advanced command and control suite, the Tian-Zong quickly exceeded its intended role. Its exceptional electronics allow battalion-level coordination while its stealthy profile makes it difficult to engage at range, earning it a reputation as one of the most dangerous heavy command 'Mechs in the Inner Sphere.

The design became the preferred mount of elite formations including the Death Commandos and Warrior Houses, serving as the Capellan Confederation's premier command 'Mech for over half a century. Ongoing production at Hellespont 'Mech Works has ensured a steady supply of upgraded variants incorporating the latest advances in Capellan military science.

The Tian-Zong's combination of stealth armor, electronic warfare capabilities, and devastating firepower makes it a formidable opponent at any range. Its Hellespont Lite II stealth armor works in concert with an Angel ECM suite, rendering the 'Mech extremely difficult to detect and target. This is a critical advantage for a design meant to operate on the flanks and behind enemy lines with shadow lances. The paired Mydron Concussor Gauss rifles deliver crushing long-range firepower without generating appreciable heat, while the Ceres Arms Striker light particle projection cannons provide accurate medium-range support. This weapons mix allows sustained engagement without taxing the 'Mech's heat management systems, leaving its pilot free to concentrate on battlefield coordination.

The Rawlings 300 XL engine propels the seventy-five-ton chassis to a respectable top speed of 64 kph, adequate for keeping pace with medium 'Mech formations. The endo-composite internal structure saves weight allocated to the heavy armor protection and weapons payload. However, the design's reliance on an extralight engine creates vulnerability in the side torsos, and its lack of jump jets limits tactical flexibility in close terrain. The small cockpit fitted to later production variants also increases pilot fatigue during prolonged engagements.

The Tian-Zong entered production in 3090 at Hellespont 'Mech Works on Sian, quickly earning its place as the Capellan Confederation's foremost command 'Mech. Originally conceived for shadow lance operations, its combination of stealth, firepower, and command electronics made it irresistible to elite formations. The Death Commandos and Warrior Houses adopted the design almost immediately, and within a decade the Tian-Zong had become synonymous with Capellan heavy command assets.

During the siege of Victoria by Armed Forces of the Federated Suns, Warrior House Kamata demonstrated the Tian-Zong's devastating potential. Using stolen encryption keys, a force comprised principally of Tian-Zongs slipped behind enemy lines during a unit rotation between battered elements of the Sixth Syrtis Fusiliers and the reconstituted Forty-second Avalon Hussars. The Warrior House maneuvered two companies of shadow lances into a gap in the Davion lines, catching the AFFS regiments mid-rotation. Their combined volley felled a full company of 'Mechs, while a second volley disabled or destroyed another dozen. Both regiments broke and ran before regrouping for a counterattack, by which time the Warrior House had withdrawn behind cover.

On Arboris, elements of the First McCarron's Armored Cavalry used the Tian-Zong to delay a company of Hastati Sentinels. Commanding a single shadow lance and a platoon of light tanks, a Capellan officer used convenient weather and varying engagement ranges to repeatedly ambush the Sentinels' patrols, throwing them off-guard each time. This resourceful use of the Tian-Zong's stealth and command capabilities tied down a significantly larger force for weeks until additional Capellan troops arrived.

During Operation Tiamat in 3149, the Fifth McCarron's Armored Cavalry teamed with Warrior House Imarra to capture Liberty. On the island of Dendez, Tian-Zong pilots of the Fifth MAC held defensive positions against a Republic Armed Forces unit identified as Stone's Fury. Despite being surprised by advanced RISC weaponry, the Tian-Zong's firepower proved decisive in several engagements, with Silver Bullet Gauss rifle shards piercing enemy cockpits at close range.

By the ilClan era, Hellespont 'Mech Works had introduced a new generation of Tian-Zong variants leveraging the Capellan Confederation's success in replicating the Star League-era Chameleon light polarization shield. These newer models traded stealth armor for lighter protection combined with the Chameleon system, freeing weight for heavier weaponry and, in some variants, jump capability. The acquisition of Clan-grade weapons through trade with the Skate Khanate further expanded the Tian-Zong's tactical versatility, ensuring the design's continued relevance on the battlefields of the thirty-second century.

The Timber Wolf is a 75-ton Clan heavy OmniMech introduced in 2945 by Clan Wolf, designed as part of a second-generation OmniMech triad alongside the Gargoyle and Naga to replace the aging Woodsman. Where the Gargoyle provided speed and the Naga offered fire-support capability, the Timber Wolf represented a near-perfect synthesis of firepower, protection, and mobility that instantly established it as the most coveted OmniMech in Clan space. Clan Wolf jealously guarded production rights to the design, successfully defending them through numerous Trials of Possession, and until the Clan Invasion of the Inner Sphere in 3049, manufacturing was limited to a single facility on Strana Mechty.

Designated "Mad Cat" by Inner Sphere forces after a targeting computer alternated between Marauder and Catapult identification codes when first attempting to classify the unknown design, the Timber Wolf has since become the most recognizable symbol of Clan military power and remains one of the most feared OmniMechs ever produced.

Built on a Type W3 Endo Steel chassis and powered by a Starfire 375 XL engine, the Timber Wolf achieves a maximum speed of 86 kph, exceptional for a heavy OmniMech. Twelve tons of Composite A-2 Ferro-Fibrous armor provide protection approaching that of many assault-class designs, though a notable weakness exists in the cockpit canopy area, where exceptionally large ferroglass viewports offer below-average ballistic protection to the MechWarrior. The chassis dedicates 27.5 tons to pod space, providing commanders with extraordinary flexibility in tailoring the design to mission requirements.

In its Primary configuration, the Timber Wolf mounts a devastating combination of energy and missile weaponry that is effective across all engagement ranges. A pair of ER Large Lasers and twin LRM-20 racks form the backbone of its long-range firepower, capable of stripping armor from targets at extreme distances. As engagements close, two ER Medium Lasers, a Medium Pulse Laser, and a pair of Machine Guns provide withering short-range fire. Fifteen double heat sinks manage the considerable thermal output, though sustained alpha strikes will test even this capacity. The Khan Series communications system and Series III OPT targeting and tracking system provide the MechWarrior with enhanced battlefield awareness and improved accuracy at medium ranges.

The Timber Wolf's true strength lies in the synergy between its speed, firepower, and armor. It can dictate engagement ranges against slower opponents while carrying enough armament to threaten designs well above its weight class. This combination proved devastating during Operation Revival, where Inner Sphere forces found themselves facing a heavy OmniMech that could outmaneuver their medium designs while outgunning their assaults.

The Timber Wolf was born from Clan Wolf's ambitious program to replace the first-generation Woodsman OmniMech with three specialized successors. Entering production in 2945 at Wolf Clan Site #2 on Strana Mechty, the design immediately proved its worth in Clan Trials, and every Clan quickly recognized its extraordinary potential. Clan Wolf successfully defended exclusive production rights through a long series of Trials of Possession, ensuring that other Clans could only acquire the design through trade, gifts, or battlefield salvage. This monopoly made the Timber Wolf a powerful bargaining chip in inter-Clan politics and a symbol of Wolf dominance throughout the Golden Century and beyond.

The Timber Wolf's reputation was cemented during Operation Revival in 3049, when it became the first Clan OmniMech encountered by Inner Sphere forces. The Fourth Wolf Guard and Thirteenth Cruiser Cluster deployed the design to devastating effect, and ComStar analysts struggled to classify a machine that defied everything they understood about BattleMech design. Inner Sphere MechWarriors found their equipment woefully inferior when facing the Timber Wolf, and the design quickly came to symbolize the Clans' overwhelming technical superiority. Much of Clan Wolf's success during the invasion was built on the Timber Wolf's dominance of the battlefield.

The Timber Wolf continued to see extensive service through the Refusal War and into the era of the Word of Blake Jihad, remaining the premier frontline OmniMech of Clan Wolf's touman. However, the design's fortunes shifted dramatically following the Wars of Reaving, which severed ties between the Inner Sphere Clans and the Homeworlds. The Wolf Clan Site #2 on Strana Mechty passed through Clan Coyote ownership during the Jihad era and eventually fell to uncertain Clan control. Meanwhile, WC Site 1 on Arc-Royal, which had produced the Timber Wolf since the Civil War era, was destroyed during the Blakist assault in 3072, dealing a devastating blow to the Wolves' production capacity.

By 3080, the surviving W-7 Facilities on Weingarten were reduced to building Timber Wolves by hand, with some components individually machined due to missing manufacturing data evacuated from the Homeworlds. Attrition vastly outstripped supply, and the Wolves increasingly turned to other designs to fill their depleted ranks. The Timber Wolf's fortunes only recovered when Alaric Ward forged the Wolf Empire. Leaving the W-7 Facilities to Clan Hell's Horses, Ward ordered the Kallon Weapon Industries plant on Thermopolis retooled for Timber Wolf production, restoring the iconic design to prominence within the Wolf touman. The Kallon facility, operational by the ilClan era, ensured the Timber Wolf would remain the symbol of Clan Wolf's martial identity for generations to come.

text.deployment: Alternate Configuration A is configured for intermediate to short-range combat, mounting a pair of large pulse lasers and two medium pulse lasers as its primary energy weapons. A pair of seven-tube Multi-Missile Launchers with two tons of ammunition provides flexible fire support across multiple range brackets, allowing the pilot to select optimal ammunition types for the engagement.

Alternate Configuration C mounts a Class 5 Rotary Autocannon as its primary weapon, supported by a pair of extended-range medium lasers, a Streak SRM-6, an ER Small Laser, and a Large Re-Engineered Laser. Three tons of autocannon ammunition and one ton of Streak ammunition provide adequate supply for extended operations, making this a well-rounded configuration effective across multiple engagement ranges.

Alternate Configuration D is specifically designed to counter 'Mechs equipped with reflective armor, mounting four medium re-engineered lasers alongside a Clan-specification LB-10X Autocannon and Clan ER PPC. The combination of kinetic and re-engineered laser weapons ensures effective damage delivery regardless of the target's armor type, with three tons of autocannon ammunition stored in the CASE-protected right torso.

Alternate Configuration A prioritizes long-range engagement with an ER PPC and Ultra Autocannon/10, both linked to a targeting computer for increased accuracy. A Streak SRM-6 provides close-range defense, while a Guardian ECM Suite protects against electronic warfare. Four jump jets grant a hundred-and-twenty meter jump capability, and an additional double heat sink helps manage the considerable thermal load, making this configuration effective at controlling engagement distances.

Alternate Configuration B serves as a sustained fire support platform, pairing an ER PPC with three Rotary Autocannon/2s capable of maintaining withering volumes of fire. Two extended-range medium lasers supplement the arsenal at closer ranges, while four additional double heat sinks ensure the 'Mech can maintain its rate of fire without overheating during prolonged engagements.

The BLO configuration is a modification used by the Blessed Order's revived First Division. Based on the Prime loadout, it removes the Streak SRM-4 launcher and its ammunition to accommodate an Improved C3 Computer, enhancing the formation's ability to coordinate fire through networked targeting data. The retained Gauss rifle, pulse lasers, and targeting computer ensure the 'Mech remains a potent combatant while serving as a critical network node.

Alternate Configuration C is configured for devastating close-range combat, centering its firepower around an LB 20-X Autocannon capable of firing both solid and cluster ammunition. Five medium pulse lasers and an extended-range medium laser provide overwhelming short-range firepower, while a single ER PPC offers long-range defense. Four jump jets provide tactical mobility, allowing the 'Mech to close with opponents or exploit terrain.

Alternate Configuration D emphasizes sustained long-range direct fire, mounting a pair of Light Gauss Rifles in the torso locations and a Large X-Pulse Laser in each arm. This loadout provides consistent damage output at extended ranges without the ammunition dependency of heavier autocannon configurations, though it sacrifices short-range punch compared to other variants.

Alternate Configuration E is purpose-built for command operations, mounting a C3 master computer to coordinate lance-level fire. A Guardian ECM Suite provides electronic protection for the formation, while offensive armament includes a pair of Artemis IV-enhanced LRM-15 launchers, an ER PPC, two medium pulse lasers, and a small laser. This configuration prioritizes the Templar's role as a formation command platform over individual combat power.

Alternate Configuration F serves as another command-oriented variant, carrying a C3 master computer alongside a Heavy PPC and Light Gauss Rifle for significant long-range firepower. Three medium pulse lasers handle closer engagements, and four jump jets provide the mobility needed to maintain optimal positioning for directing lance operations and coordinating formation fire.

Alternate Configuration G appears designed for long-range direct fire support or anti-aircraft duties, mounting three LB 2-X autocannons alongside an ER PPC and Light Gauss Rifle. A C3 slave unit enables the sharing of targeting data with lancemates, enhancing the collective accuracy of the formation while the configuration provides sustained suppressive fire at extended ranges.

Alternate Configuration H combines missile and energy firepower with networking capability, carrying an MRM-30 launcher with Apollo Fire Control System in each arm for devastating medium-range salvos. A pair of Light PPCs and an ER Flamer round out the weapons suite, with a targeting computer enhancing energy weapon accuracy. A C3 slave unit provides data-sharing capability, and four jump jets grant the mobility to maintain effective engagement ranges.

Alternate Configuration I focuses on raw firepower and heat management, mounting two Heavy PPCs and a Gauss Rifle as its primary armament. Fifteen double heat sinks provide the cooling capacity necessary to sustain fire from both PPCs simultaneously, while a C3 slave unit integrates the 'Mech into lance-level targeting networks. This configuration trades flexibility for sheer destructive output at range.

Alternate Configuration R stands as a Dark Age era upgrade incorporating Clan-specification weapons, mounting twin Clan ER PPCs and a Clan LB 10-X autocannon for devastating long-range firepower. Five medium re-engineered lasers provide close-range punch that remains effective against reflective armor. This configuration reflects the increasing availability of Clan technology to Inner Sphere powers during the later Dark Age period.

Alternate Configuration U is specifically designed for underwater operations, equipped with four Underwater Maneuvering Units and a BattleMech HarJel System to prevent hull breaches. Offensive armament includes a large pulse laser, three medium pulse lasers, an SRT-6 and LRT-10 torpedo launcher for submerged combat. A C3 slave unit maintains coordination with friendly forces in the limited-visibility underwater environment.

Alternate Configuration A shifts the Tenshi's focus to medium-range combat with devastating energy firepower. Three Large Variable Speed Pulse Lasers, distributed across both arms and the center torso, deliver concentrated damage at varying ranges. An Apollo-guided MRM-30 launcher with CASE II-protected ammunition provides additional striking power and volume of fire. Five extra Double Heat Sinks and a Coolant Pod help manage the substantial thermal output of this energy-heavy loadout, though sustained alpha strikes remain challenging even with the additional cooling capacity.

This logistical burden is the design's most significant drawback, requiring dedicated technical teams and extended maintenance windows that can strain a formation's operational tempo during fast-moving campaigns.
text.deployment: Alternate Configuration B is built around a pair of TSEMP Cannons, one mounted in each arm, capable of crippling enemy electronics systems and shutting down opposing 'Mechs entirely. A Heavy PPC provides long-range direct-fire punch, while paired Streak SRM-6 launchers and Medium Pulse Lasers fill close-combat roles against targets already staggered by TSEMP strikes. Three Jump Jets grant the B configuration a mobility advantage unusual for an assault 'Mech of this tonnage, allowing it to navigate difficult terrain and achieve firing positions that would otherwise be inaccessible.

The R configuration employs a mix of Inner Sphere and Clan technologies to create a long-range indirect fire support platform. Twin Extended Long-Range Missile 20 launchers backed by six tons of ammunition can saturate targets at extreme distances well beyond the reach of most conventional weapons. Five Clan-manufactured ER Medium Lasers provide accurate backup firepower at closer ranges, giving this variant some protection against units that manage to close the distance. This configuration transforms the Tenshi from a direct-combat assault 'Mech into a bombardment platform best employed behind friendly lines.

text.deployment: A subvariant of the TNS-6S produced at StarCorps' Loburg facility, this variant replaces the C3 slave unit with a CASE II system to protect against ammunition explosions in the LRM-laden right arm. This trade sacrifices networked targeting capability for improved pilot survivability, a pragmatic modification reflecting field experience with the -6S design.
text.battleHistory:
The Thanatos traces its origins to StarCorps Industries' experience producing licensed OmniMechs from Luthien Armor Works. By 3060, StarCorps was manufacturing Black Hawk KUs, Avatars, and Sunders across four worlds, building the institutional knowledge necessary to design their own Omni-technology platforms. The Thanatos emerged alongside the Manteuffel OmniVehicle as the first fruits of this initiative. When neither the LAAF nor the AFFS expressed interest in the OmniMech version, StarCorps converted it into a standard BattleMech, a decision that proved shrewd, winning contracts from both militaries that carried production from 3061 into the next decade.

The Thanatos found its niche in heavy cavalry formations, operating alongside similarly fast designs like the Argus, Barghest, Falconer, and Rakshasa. It displaced aging Quickdraws in units such as the First Federated Suns Armored Cavalry and the Alliance Jaegers. StarCorps also marketed the design to mercenary commands, with buyers ranging from the prestigious Eridani Light Horse to smaller outfits.

Production survived the Jihad at both the Crofton and Loburg facilities. The Jihad era produced the TNS-6T refit, which replaced the original's missile and laser loadout with a snub-nose PPC and multi-missile launcher. Both factories began producing the -6T as a standard model during the 3080s, with Loburg also offering the CASE II-equipped TNS-6S2 subvariant.

During the Dark Age, the Thanatos continued to serve the Armed Forces of the Federated Suns and the Lyran Commonwealth Armed Forces. In 3146, Republic Armed Forces technicians developed an upgraded variant using Clan-specification weapons during a stopover on Terra. These specifications were passed to StarCorps on Crofton, which began producing the TNS-7D for the AFFS, featuring an all-ClanTech weapons suite that dramatically improved the design's reach and accuracy. StarCorps subsequently offered the TNS-7D2 subvariant, trading electronic warfare capability for an Artemis V fire-control system.

Though some observers considered the Thanatos as never quite fulfilling the potential StarCorps originally envisioned, the design proved durable and adaptable enough to remain in continuous production for nearly a century, proof of the soundness of its underlying chassis and the flexibility of its weapon bays.

text.deployment: Originally developed as a Jihad-era field refit, this variant entered full production during the 3080s at both the Crofton and Loburg facilities. CASE II protects the ammunition stores in the right arm. The design was also offered as a refit package for existing Thanatos chassis.

An advanced electronics package enhances weapon accuracy while shielding against enemy targeting systems.

text.overview:
The Thunderbolt was first produced in 2491 by Earthwerks Limited on Tikonov for the Capellan Confederation, representing the heaviest BattleMech the fledgling manufacturer could produce at the time. Designed from the outset as a planetary assault platform, the Thunderbolt, affectionately known as the T-Bolt or the Thud, established itself as one of the most formidable heavy ’Mechs of the Age of War. The design impressed the Confederation’s neighbors sufficiently that Earthwerks expanded into the Free Worlds League within fifteen years, establishing production on Keystone. Olivetti Weaponry on Sudeten, Taurus Territorial Industries, and Vandenberg Mechanized Industries on Pinard further broadened the manufacturing base across the Inner Sphere and Periphery.

Renowned for its varied arsenal, exceptional armor protection, and an easily modified chassis, the Thunderbolt has remained in continuous production for over five centuries. Periodic updates have ensured the design remains competitive against newer heavy ’Mechs, and its ubiquity is such that virtually every military force in the Inner Sphere and Periphery fields at least one Thunderbolt in its ranks.
text.capabilities:
The Thunderbolt’s greatest tactical asset is its eclectic weapons mix, which allows it to engage effectively at virtually any range. A Sunglow Type 2 large laser and Delta Dart LRM-15 launcher provide respectable long-range firepower, while three Diverse Optics Type 18 medium lasers mounted in a tight cluster and a Bical SRM-2 launcher deliver punishing close-range salvos. A pair of Voelkers 200 machine guns rounds out the arsenal for anti-infantry work. This combination enables the Thunderbolt to serve capably in roles ranging from fire support to brawling, a versatility few designs of its era can match.

Thirteen tons of Ryerson 150 armor provide protection that rivals or exceeds many assault ’Mechs, giving MechWarriors considerable confidence in sustained engagements. The Magna 260 fusion engine propels the chassis to a respectable sixty-four kilometers per hour, adequate for maintaining formation with most heavy lances. The Thunderbolt also features an exceptionally roomy cockpit compared to similarly sized designs, reducing pilot fatigue during prolonged campaigns.

The Thunderbolt’s well-known weakness is its inadequate heat dissipation. With only fifteen heat sinks struggling to manage the thermal output of its numerous energy weapons and missile systems, MechWarriors must carefully manage their rate of fire or risk shutdown and ammunition cook-off. Many commanders order their Thunderbolts into bodies of water at the outset of engagements, allowing pilots to fire their weapons more aggressively than the design’s cooling systems would otherwise permit.
text.deployment: The TDR-5SS1 represents the original Steiner variant of the Thunderbolt, predating the more refined TDR-5SS. This earlier model carried the same Kreuss PPC as its successor but retained a flamer and the machine guns at the cost of fewer heat sinks. The resulting thermal management challenges proved significant enough that subsequent production dropped the flamer and machine guns entirely in favor of additional heat sinks, producing the better-known TDR-5SS. Few TDR-5SS1 models survived in identifiable condition long enough to be distinguished from their successors in field reports.
text.battleHistory:
The Thunderbolt’s origins trace to 2491, when Earthwerks Limited on Tikonov produced the primitive TDR-1C under the guidance of engineer Sarkia Menendez. Despite the Capellan Confederation’s relative inexperience with BattleMech technology, the design set records in development time and immediately proved its worth as a planetary assault platform. The upgraded TDR-5S entered production on Keystone within fifteen years, while Olivetti Weaponry on Sudeten began manufacturing its own line. This broad production base established the Thunderbolt as a traditionally Capellan design that nonetheless became most closely associated with House Steiner and House Marik, the two largest producers during the Succession Wars.

The Succession Wars tested the Thunderbolt’s durability across centuries of grinding attrition. During the Second Succession War, Earthwerks on Tikonov attempted to preserve Star League technology through the TDR-5L, a downgraded Royal variant, but further industrial decline forced the creation of the even more simplified TDR-5LS by 2850. Both variants eventually vanished from production lines as the technology to build them was lost. Meanwhile, the standard TDR-5S continued to serve in virtually every major engagement, including the Battle of Chesterton in 2828 where Thunderbolts of the Seventh Tikonov Lancers clashed with Davion Crucis Lancers in brutal close-quarters fighting.

The Clan Invasion brought upheaval when Clan Jade Falcon conquered Sudeten, capturing Olivetti’s production lines. Though the Falcons continued producing Thunderbolts using what they considered outdated technology into 3054, the loss stung the Inner Sphere. Earthwerks responded with modernized variants, most notably the TDR-7M in 3049 and the ambitious TDR-9M in 3067. The latter sparked a legal confrontation with Irian BattleMechs Unlimited, which had introduced the Tempest as the Thunderbolt’s replacement. The Word of Blake brokered a compromise through a combat trial, which the TDR-9M won decisively, securing continued production and Blakist military contracts.

Trellshire Heavy Industries on Adelaide emerged as an important new manufacturer after barely surviving bankruptcy during the Clan Invasion. Initially producing retrotech garrison models during the Jihad, Trellshire gradually expanded to become the Lyran Commonwealth’s primary Thunderbolt supplier with the TDR-7S in 3091. Blackwell Industries also contributed the TDR-9W for Wolf’s Dragoons, drawing on a Golden Century-era Clan refit package. Earthwerks’ Tikonov facility continued production through multiple regime changes, including Republic of the Sphere control and the Capellan reconquest of 3145, where locally built Thunderbolts played decisive roles during Operation Golden Fortress and subsequent battles for the planet.

Nearing its seventh century on the battlefield, the Thunderbolt remains one of the most recognizable and widely produced BattleMechs in existence. Its durability and adaptability have ensured that no Inner Sphere or Periphery military is without at least one Thunderbolt in its inventory, whether obtained by purchase, license, or salvage.

text.deployment: A product of the Capellan Confederation's success in replicating the Star League-era Chameleon light polarization shield during the 3140s, this variant fundamentally rethinks the Tian-Zong's defensive approach. Replacing the stealth armor with Hellespont Lite light ferro-fibrous protection and mounting a Chameleon system, the design gains equivalent stealth capability with reduced weight and heat burden. The fragile Hellespont Type TZ-Lite composite internal structure saves additional tonnage, allowing one of the standard Gauss rifles to be replaced with a Mydron Shattershot Silver Bullet Gauss rifle. Inspired by engagements against Oriente Carronades, the Silver Bullet's cluster munitions exploit holes punched by the standard Gauss rifle, creating a devastating one-two combination.

Building upon the original TNZ-N1 as its foundation, this variant incorporates the Chameleon light polarization shield and light ferro-fibrous armor of the newer generation while taking a dramatically different tactical direction. One Gauss rifle is replaced with a Clan-grade extended-range PPC sourced from the Skate Khanate, and a TAG system is fitted for semi-guided munition coordination. The extralight engine is exchanged for a lighter-model fusion engine, and four jump jets provide the Tian-Zong with vertical mobility for the first time. Though the mixed weapons loadout requires more careful heat management, the combination of jump capability, indirect fire coordination, and Clan-grade weaponry makes this variant one of the most tactically flexible in the lineup.

The most heavily armed variant of the Tian-Zong, this experimental model replaces both Gauss rifles with Clan-manufactured class-10 Ultra autocannons dating back to the Golden Century. Nearly castoffs by Clan standards, these weapons represent an enormous upgrade for the ClanTech-starved Capellan military. A compact gyro and small cockpit free the internal volume necessary for the autocannons and their ammunition, while CASE II protects the ammo-bearing side torsos from catastrophic detonation. The Hellespont Type TZ-Lite composite structure and Chameleon light polarization shield maintain stealth capability without stealth armor. With fifteen double heat sinks managing the substantial heat load, it features the most firepower and heaviest armor protection of any Tian-Zong variant.

text.deployment: This variant configuration was developed for the Blessed Order's revived Com Guard First Division, specifically the Unending Faith III formation. The Blessed Order was a secretive neo-Blakist faction within ComStar that covertly rebuilt the First Division's military capability during the Dark Age era. Each arm carries an ER PPC for powerful long-range direct fire, while Streak SRM-6 racks in the side torsos provide efficient close-range engagement capability with two tons of ammunition. An ER Small Laser in the center torso rounds out the weapons suite. The configuration's most notable feature is its electronics package: TAG in the right torso enables artillery designation, while a Light Active Probe and Inner Sphere Improved C3 Computer in the left torso provide network warfare capability, reflecting the Com Guard doctrine of coordinated combined-arms operations. The Blessed Order and its First Division were ultimately destroyed by Republic Armed Forces on Epsilon Eridani in 3141, making this configuration a rare footnote in the Timber Wolf's long service history.

Alternate Configuration U adapts the Timber Wolf for hostile underwater environments. A BattleMech HarJel system protects the torso sections from hull breaches, while four Underwater Maneuvering Units allow the design to cruise through water at 43 kph. The weapons loadout mirrors the Primary configuration's philosophy with a pair of Artemis IV-enhanced LRT-15 torpedo launchers on the shoulders and an ER Large Laser with an ER Micro Laser in each arm. This configuration demonstrates the Timber Wolf chassis's adaptability, extending its operational envelope to naval and amphibious operations where conventional OmniMechs cannot operate.

text.overview:
The Titan is a hundred-ton assault BattleMech prototype originally designed for the Star League Defense Force in 2765, intended to serve as a devastating close-range brawler. Developed by Blankenburg Technologies on Terra, the design never advanced beyond prototype testing before the upheaval of the Amaris Civil War halted all further development. The specifications that General Aleksandr Kerensky himself reviewed reportedly influenced his later commissioning of the Devastator to address perceived shortcomings in the Titan concept.

The Titan's legacy far outlived its brief prototype phase. Recovered by Federated Suns forces in 3023, the original specifications inspired both the radically redesigned Grand Titan produced by Earthwerks and the more faithful Titan II built by Kressly WarWorks for the Word of Blake. Centuries after its initial development, the Titan itself was finally brought into limited production during the Dark Age era.
text.capabilities:
Weighing in at a full hundred tons, the Titan was designed around a Vlar 300 standard fusion engine that limits its top speed to fifty-four kilometers per hour. While slow even by assault 'Mech standards, the use of a standard engine provides exceptional survivability, as the 'Mech can continue operating even after catastrophic torso damage. Nineteen tons of standard armor give the Titan formidable protection across its frame.

The original armament centers on twin PPCs providing long-range striking power, supplemented by six medium lasers and a battery of short-range missiles (four SRM-4 launchers and an SRM-6) for devastating close-range salvos. This weapon mix reflects a brawler philosophy that demands the pilot close to effective range to bring the full arsenal to bear. The twenty-two single heat sinks proved insufficient for sustained fire with all weapons, forcing MechWarriors to carefully manage their engagement profile. Despite these heat management challenges, the Titan's combination of rugged construction and heavy firepower represented a sound assault platform that simply arrived at the wrong moment in history.
text.deployment: The TI-1Ak Highshooter is a custom named configuration of the Titan platform. As a non-standard modification, the Highshooter represents an individual or small-unit adaptation of the base Titan design to suit a specific tactical preference or operational requirement. Detailed technical specifications and the precise origin of this named variant remain limited in available records.
text.battleHistory:
The Titan's origins trace to the final years of the Star League, when Blankenburg Technologies on Terra developed the prototype to specifications reviewed by General Aleksandr Kerensky himself. The design was intended to fill an assault 'Mech role emphasizing close-range dominance, but the onset of the Amaris Civil War in 2766 disrupted all further development. The prototype facilities were either destroyed or abandoned during the conflict, and the Titan was consigned to history as another promising design lost to the chaos of the era.

The design resurfaced when Armed Forces of the Federated Suns forces recovered the original specifications in 3023. The New Avalon Institute of Science reportedly conducted limited experiments with the design, producing a small number of prototypes, though full-scale production was never attempted. The recovered data proved more valuable as inspiration than as a production blueprint, Vining Engineering and Salvage Team used it as the foundation for the Grand Titan, while the Word of Blake later directed Kressly WarWorks to produce the more faithful Titan II.

The Titan itself finally entered limited production during the Dark Age era, when Kressly WarWorks applied the original NAIS-derived specifications to their production line on Epsilon Eridani, manufacturing updated variants for the Republic Armed Forces. These modernized versions incorporated double heat sinks and CASE protection while retaining the core design philosophy that had made the original prototype appealing to Kerensky's engineers over two centuries earlier.
